clinician.final_diagnosis: confirming sinonasal intestinal mucinous type adenocarcinoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old male presented with chronic globalized headache, nasal obstruction, anosmia, and recent left-side visual loss. Neurological exam confirmed anosmia and left visual impairment. Brain MRI and CT revealed a T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense anterior cranial fossa lesion arising from the left ethmoid and sphenoid sinuses, compressing the left optic structures, and heterogeneous masses. Biopsy of the mass showed irregular tissue fragments with variable-sized glands lined by single to pseudostratified columnar cells with apical mucinous cytoplasm embedded in a desmoplastic stroma, consistent with adenocarcinoma with mucinous and intestinal features. The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the tumor via bicoronal skin incision and bifrontal craniotomy. Postoperatively, behavioral changes resolved, left vision improved, nasal obstruction and snoring improved, and epistaxis resolved, though anosmia persisted.

Neurological examination confirmed bilateral anosmia and left eye visual impairment (hand movement at 30 cm).
Brain MRI showed a T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense anterior cranial fossa lesion arising from the left ethmoid and sphenoid sinuses, compressing the left optic structures.
Brain CT demonstrated heterogeneous hypo- to isodense masses in the sinonasal region.

Biopsy revealed irregular tissue fragments consisting of variable-sized glands lined by single to pseudostratified columnar cells with apical mucinous cytoplasm embedded in a desmoplastic stroma, consistent with adenocarcinoma with mucinous and intestinal features.
The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the tumor.
Post-operative course showed improvement in vision, resolution of behavioral changes, epistaxis, nasal obstruction, and snoring.
